newsitem.title: CHINA: China shipbuilder output value up 20.5 pct in H1.
newsitem.headline: China shipbuilder output value up 20.5 pct in H1.

text.p: China's largest shipbuilder China State Shipbuilder Corp (CSSC) built vessels worth 6.32 billion yuan between January and July 1996, up 20.5 percent from the same period last year, the Xinhua news agency said on Monday.

The company produced a total of 784,000 deadweight tonnes of ships in the first six months and so far this year had received orders for building and repairing 1.6 million deadweight tonnes of ships, Xinhua said.
CSSC had done more than 900 million yuan worth of repairs on 540 vessels in the first half, an increase in value of 31.5 percent over the year-ago period, the agency said.
Foreign ships accounted for 70 percent of the ships repaired and 80 percent of the value of repairs, it said.
CSSC accounts for more than half China's production of ships, with output of 1.75 million tonnes in 1995.
In the industry as a whole, the value of ship repairs in the first half rose about 30 percent year-on-year, with low prices attracting customers from Greece, Ukraine and South Korea, it said.
CSSC had also started specialised repair work on container ships, liquefied gas ships and oil tankers, Xinhua said but gave no further details.
